derivation.canonical_behavior: Go aria2 client owns protocol mechanics with typed timeouts and malformed reply handling.

invariants: The Go RPC client owns JSON-RPC envelope mechanics and exact request/response correlation.
Authentication token material is prepended only at runtime and is redacted from returned server error messages.
Every RPC call has a bounded timeout and malformed/oversized replies fail without echoing raw response bodies.
Add/status/active/waiting/stopped/pause/unpause/remove/change options/global options/save session/shutdown/health are available through one client.
aria2 option values are encoded as strings or string arrays rather than host-dependent JSON scalar types.
RPC redirects are refused and process launch/restart ownership is outside the RPC package.
